newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila share index ends at day's high on GNP.
newsitem.headline: Manila share index ends at day's high on GNP.

text.p: Philippine shares headed higher on Friday with investors encouraged by favourable first quarter GNP figures, traders said.
The main index ended at its intra-day high, breaching the 2,800 resistance. It closed 50.84 points up, or 1.84 percent, at 2,809.45.

"Investors may have discounted the weak manufacturing sector which slowed down overall economic growth, so they've decided to bargain hunt on blue chip issues," Jidgette Valenzuela, research manager at Lippo Securities said.
First quarter GNP rose 6.1 percent against 6.9 last year.

"The Thailand comparison was a big factor in the recent slump of the market. The economic growth figures showed that we are not like Thailand and this improved the market's fragile sentiment," said Allan Araullo, vice-president at Regina Capital Development Corp.
The property sub-index posted the biggest gain among the market's six sub-indices, rising 3.05 percent to close at 1,357.29 points.
Propping up the market were blue chips Ayala Land Inc, Metrobank, Ayala Corp B and PLDT.
"I think that there should really be a consolidation by next week after this seven day run-up. But it will not hit the bottom of 2,450 points," said Carl Valentin, analyst at Asia Pacific Capital.
